newsitem.title: THAILAND: Concrete Construction sees Thai revenue up.
newsitem.headline: Concrete Construction sees Thai revenue up.

text.p: Concrete Constructions (Thailand) Ltd, the Thai unit of Germany's Walter-Bau AG, said on Monday it sees revenues doubling to three billion baht (US$116 million) in 1997 from 1.5 billion last year.

Its general manager John Bradbury said on Monday that the firm now generates most of its income from construction of condominiums and factories in Thailand but believed its engineering activities, hold the key to sustained corporate growth.
He did not give profit figures.
"We are interested in infrastructure, which is where we are going to push, and we see good growth opportunities in solid and waste water treatment as well as in power projects," he told reporters.
The company was looking to form joint ventures with local partners to enter bids on expressway and small power producer (SPP) and independent power producer (IPP) projects, company officials said.
Revenues from engineering activities were scheduled to contribute 1 billion baht in 1997, and 25 percent year on year growth was achievable in the medium term, they added.
The company currently has 12 general construction, and two engineering projects ongoing, including a waste water collection scheme in Bangkok.
It was also looking at further waste water projects, as well as solid waste projects for the Bangkok Metropolitan Authority, civil operation manager Eleftherios Panayiotou said.
The company, which is 51 percent owned by Thailand retail shopping giant Central Group, said it would complete work on Central's fire-ravaged Chidlom Road department store in Bangkok by mid-1997.
Concrete Constructions (Thailand) Ltd is owned by Concrete Constructions Australia, 75 percent of which was bought by German constructor Walter-Bau AG in 1995.
